facts.fact: Shim pack stacking orientation is critical and cannot be inverted. AUTHORITATIVE order (per the CORRECT_Order reference video): thick spacer (cod.92203637) goes down first, then the shims, then the thin spacer (cod.191713A1) on top. NOTE: this phase-8 video narration said 'thin one down first' — that is the imprecise shop narration that this check guards against; always defer to the correct-order reference (thick -> shims -> thin).

Authoritative assembly order on the pinion shaft (per the CORRECT_Order reference video): thick spacer (cod.92203637) down first, then the shims, then the thin spacer (cod.191713A1) on top — NOT 'thin shim first'. The phase-8 narration's 'thin shim, then thick spacer' is exactly the common mix-up to avoid; always build thick -> shims -> thin.

citation.transcript_quote: Thin shim. And then... Thick spacer.

facts.fact: A feeler gauge is used before pressing to verify the shim stack height is within acceptable range — the gauge should go in about the correct amount to confirm the assembly is okay.

citation.transcript_quote: Feeler gauge. Tells us if it's okay. If it goes in about that much.

facts.fact: After placing the snap ring, you must verify it is fully flat and seated inside the groove before pressing, using a dedicated tool to confirm seating.

citation.transcript_quote: We must make sure it's flat and it's inside the groove. We use our tool.

facts.fact: Before pressing with the punch fixture, use a check tool to verify the assembly moves smoothly all the way down; if it does not move smoothly, the assembly is not mounted correctly and must be corrected.

citation.transcript_quote: If it doesn't move smoothly, then it's not mounted correct.

facts.fact: A go/no-go gauge is used as part of the assembly verification; the 'no go' side must not pass and the 'go' side must pass to confirm correctness.

The phase 8 procedure picture only shows the final pressed result and does not document the intermediate steps of installing the snap ring or shims, so workers must rely on verbal knowledge not captured in the formal instructions.
